result.title: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
result.summary: As AI systems are increasingly used to automate AI R&D, misaligned systems could sabotage research intended to improve model safety and alignment. To stress-test defenses against such sabotage, we use a human expert as a proxy saboteur on AI safety research. We conduct a red-team/blue-team game where a human researcher runs AI safety experiments from scratch and auditors try to tell which were sabotaged and how. Given access to the full research transcript and the ability to run experiments, human auditors mostly fail to distinguish sabotaged from benign research: they achieve an AUROC of 0.59, not significantly better than chance, and fully identify the specific sabotage in only 17% of cases. Despite not being allowed to run experiments, the best frontier models outperform human auditors (Fable 5.1: AUROC 0.73, 32% full identification) within noise and weaker models perform comparably. When the saboteur chooses which experiments are attacked, rather than being required to sabotage every question given, sabotage identification drops further. Our results suggest that research sabotage by expert-level agents is difficult to detect with current auditing methods and provide a new setting for studying research sabotage.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文让人类专家充当「破坏者」在AI安全研究中植入蓄意破坏，构建红蓝对抗审计场景，测试人类审计员与前沿模型能否从完整研究记录中判断哪些实验被破坏及具体手法。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作实质在检验「仅凭完整推理记录能否还原真实计算意图」，这与LVR中显式trace的可监督性、以及把推理转入latent状态后证据可审计性与评价成本的问题可能相关，可供核查其审计设定是否能迁移为trace/latent状态忠实性的评测思路。
